title: A Signal for the Vector
premise: Astrid Yarrow, a terraformer hauling seed-cargo through contested orbits, has spent five years hiding his past as the fleet's most wanted signal analyst. When the deep-space vessel Meridian returns with its crew aged backward and carrying a transmission that could ignite war between the two fleets, Astrid recognizes the signal as a forgery—one he himself designed years ago as an insurance policy. To expose it, he must reveal who he was, betraying the found family of gardeners who trust him, while the forger—his former mentor Vess Kade—hunts him to protect the fragile peace built on her lie. In the end, Astrid broadcasts the truth not to destroy the peace but to rebuild it honestly, sacrificing his anonymity and nearly his life, and chooses to stay with the unborn colony's garden rather than return to either fleet.
about_author: Ines Galloway is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town where she keeps a failing greenhouse and insists it is thriving.

chapters.title: Seed Cargo
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He ferries genetic stock to an orbital greenhouse meant for colonists not yet conceived, trading small kindnesses with dock crews who don't ask questions. The routine is interrupted when the long-lost ship Meridian appears at the edge of contested space. Emotional beat: quiet contentment shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Back Younger
chapters.summary: POV: Juno Reyes, greenhouse botanist and Astrid's closest friend. She watches quarantine footage of the Meridian's crew—faces she knew as veterans now decades younger, memories intact. Astrid goes pale at the news and lies about why. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into unease.

chapters.title: Five Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, flashback-heavy. We learn he was Callum Yarrow, the signal architect whose forged transmission ended the Last Exchange—a war that killed forty thousand—and vanished afterward. The Meridian's return threatens everything because its captain once served under him. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: Quarantine Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Captain Ilsa Voss of the patrol frigate Halcyon. She orders the Meridian held, but its crew transmits a verified authentication code—an old military cipher only three people alive should know. One of them is dead; one is Vess Kade; one is a ghost named Callum Yarrow. Emotional beat: institutional suspicion tightening.

chapters.title: What the Garden Knows
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. She notices Astrid decrypting something on a salvaged terminal at 3 a.m., his hands shaking. When she confronts him gently, he deflects, but she recognizes the cipher notation from her academy days. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to strain against curiosity.

chapters.title: The Message Inside the Message
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He decodes the Meridian's broadcast and finds embedded instructions ordering both fleets to converge on the greenhouse station—the very place he's hidden for five years. The signal is his own forgery, updated, weaponized by someone who knows he's alive. Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: POV: Vess Kade, aboard the Meridian, biologically twenty-five again after the ship's time-dilation anomaly. She reflects on why she resurrected Astrid's old forgery: the peace it bought is rotting, and only a shared enemy can hold the fleets together. Emotional beat: righteous conviction with cracks showing.

chapters.title: Dockside Fire
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. An 'accident' destroys the greenhouse's outer ring, killing two workers. Evidence points to fleet saboteurs, inflaming tensions among the gardeners. Astrid saves Juno from a collapsing module, using reflexes no cargo hauler should have. Emotional beat: grief and the first open question about who Astrid really is.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Captain Voss's POV. She traces the authentication cipher to its origin and finds redacted files naming Callum Yarrow, presumed dead. Ordered by her own command to bury the finding, she begins quietly investigating instead. Emotional beat: duty versus conscience.

chapters.title: Confession in the Seed Vault
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Cornered by Juno among the dormant embryos, he tells her the truth: his forgery stopped a war, and its revival will start a bigger one unless he can prove it's fake. Juno must decide whether to report him or help him. Emotional beat: raw vulnerability; trust offered without guarantee.

chapters.title: The Meridian's Secret
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. It's revealed the age reversal came from experimental stasis tech the Meridian was secretly testing—a war-winning technology both fleets would kill for. Vess has been using the crew's condition as leverage, and the convergence order is her trap to seize the greenhouse as collateral. Emotional beat: cold ambition masking fear.

chapters.title: Intercept Course
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. She and Astrid rig a cargo hauler to intercept a relay buoy and broadcast a counter-signal proving the forgery. Mid-mission they're boarded by Voss's patrol, and Astrid must talk his way past a woman who has spent months hunting his ghost. Emotional beat: high-wire tension, unexpected alliance forming.

chapters.title: The Ghost Testifies
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In Voss's briefing room, he reveals himself as Callum Yarrow and demonstrates the forgery's cryptographic fingerprints. Voss believes him—but her superiors won't, because the lie is now load-bearing for the armistice. Emotional beat: vindication that changes nothing.

chapters.title: Orders to Forget
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Command strips her rank and orders Yarrow's arrest as a destabilizing element. She faces a choice: obey and let the trap close, or go rogue with the truth. She releases Astrid and burns her career behind her. Emotional beat: costly integrity.

chapters.title: Kade's Offer
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She contacts Astrid directly, offering absolution: join her, legitimize the new threat, and the fleets unite against a common enemy—peace through manufactured fear. She genuinely believes she's saving more lives than his honesty ever did. Emotional beat: seductive moral gravity.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Fleet forces arrive to 'protect' the greenhouse, effectively occupying it. Juno organizes the gardeners into passive resistance, refusing to let the unborn colony become a bargaining chip. Astrid, torn between fleeing and standing, sees what he built here is worth the exposure. Emotional beat: solidarity hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Convergence
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Both fleets arrive in orbit around the greenhouse station as Vess planned, weapons hot, each believing the other fired first. Astrid realizes the only frequency both sides still trust is the original forgery's channel. Emotional beat: brinkmanship, clock ticking.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax part one. From the greenhouse's antenna array, he hijacks the sacred channel and transmits the full proof of forgery—along with his own confession, name unhidden, voice unaltered—to both fleets simultaneously. Vess attempts to jam him; Juno and the gardeners physically shield the array. Emotional beat: self-immolation as testimony.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Garden
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, climax part two. With the truth public, both fleets waver. Vess launches a strike on the station to destroy the evidence; Voss's frigate interposes itself, taking critical damage. Astrid, exposed on the array platform, is wounded shielding Juno. Emotional beat: sacrifice meeting sacrifice.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Truth
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. The fleets stand down, humiliated and leaderless—Vess surrenders rather than let her crews die for her architecture of fear. Astrid survives, barely, and wakes to find neither fleet knows what to do with a man who broke a peace to save a future. Emotional beat: exhausted, uncertain dawn.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Facing tribunals from both fleets, he proposes instead a joint commission to verify all armistice communications—truth as infrastructure rather than martyrdom. Voss, reinstated, becomes its first witness. Vess, imprisoned, sends him a single line: 'You were always the better liar.' Emotional beat: justice negotiated, not imposed.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Juno's POV, closing. Months later, the first verified supply ships arrive carrying volunteers for the colony-to-be. Astrid, going by his real name now, works the soil beside Juno as the embryos' incubation cycle begins. He tends a garden for people not yet born—as himself. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
